q: A consultant is selecting a valve for a chilled-water balancing application where the flow rate must be adjusted repeatedly during commissioning and fine-tuned throughout the life of the building. The valve is not intended primarily for isolation, but rather for frequent throttling and accurate flow regulation. Which valve is most appropriate for this application?
n: Globe valves are made for throttling and accurate, repeated flow adjustment. Gate and ball valves are mainly for isolation. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (valves); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A high-rise residential building utilizes a basement cistern, transfer pump, and roof deck water tank. Water is distributed to the lower floors through a gravity downfeed system. Residents on the ground floor complain that faucets and handheld bidets discharge water with excessive force. The designer seeks a permanent solution that automatically maintains a safer and more consistent downstream pressure without constant operator adjustment. Which device should be specified?
n: A pressure-reducing (regulating) valve automatically holds a lower, steady downstream pressure. That is the permanent fix for high pressure on the lower floors of a downfeed system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6 (pressure-reducing valves where pressure exceeds 80 psi); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A high-rise building utilizes a roof-deck tank and gravity downfeed water distribution system. Occupants on the lower floors experience unusually strong water discharge from faucets and bidet sprayers. If left uncorrected, what is the most likely consequence of this condition?
o: Increased storage capacity of the water tank
n: Too much pressure strains fittings and seals and can cause water hammer, leading to leaks and fixture damage. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Before installing plumbing fixtures, what essential process ensures that pipes, drains and water supply lines are properly positioned and connected within walls or floors?
n: Roughing-in is installing and positioning the supply and drain piping inside walls and floors before fixtures go in. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is the minimum slope of a water supply pipe?
n: Pressurized water supply pipes need no slope, since pressure moves the water. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6 (water distribution).

q: What is the required slope for pressurized water service piping in a building's distribution system?
n: No slope is prescribed for pressurized water distribution piping. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6.

q: What is the most likely consequence when the slope of a drainage pipe is too steep?
o: Water flows too quickly, leaving solids behind and causing blockages
Flow slows down and causes backflow into fixtures
The pipe becomes self-cleaning due to increased velocity
Water and solids travel together more efficiently
n: In a pipe that is too steep, water outruns the solids and leaves them behind to build up into blockages. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (slope of horizontal drainage piping); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: In a sanitary drainage system governed by the Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (NPCP), what is the primary function of a vent stack?
o: To equalize air pressure within the drainage system and protect trap seals from siphonage
To collect stormwater from roof drains and discharge it to the sewer
To increase the flow velocity of wastewater in vertical stacks
To serve as an auxiliary waste pipe for fixtures located above the main stack
n: A vent stack equalizes air pressure in the drainage system and protects trap seals from siphonage and back-pressure. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 9 (Vents and Venting).

q: What is the primary purpose of providing a cleanout in a sanitary drainage system?
o: To increase the slope of the drainage line for faster wastewater flow
To serve as an auxiliary vent connection for fixtures on lower floors
To provide access for clearing blockages and performing maintenance inside the drainage pipe
To reduce noise transmission from wastewater flowing through the pipes
n: Cleanouts give access for clearing blockages and maintaining drain pipes. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (Cleanouts).

q: Under the National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, a cleanout is required at which of the following locations?
o: At the upper end of every vent pipe
At every change in pipe diameter
At the upper terminal of each horizontal waste or soil pipe run
n: A cleanout is required at the upper terminal of each horizontal waste or soil pipe run, among other locations. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (Cleanouts, location).

q: What 1s the primary purpose of installing a vent cap at the termination of a sanitary vent pipe?
o: To create positive pressure inside the drainage system for faster waste discharge
To serve as an anchor point for roof maintenance equipment
To prevent rainwater, debris, and small animals from entering the vent while allowing free airflow
To increase the velocity of air moving through the vent system
n: A vent cap keeps rain, debris and small animals out of the vent while letting air flow freely. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 9 (vent terminals); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Inside a toilet cistern, which component automatically controls the inflow of water and shuts off the supply once the desired water level has been reached?
n: The ball cock (fill valve) refills the cistern and shuts off the supply once the set water level is reached. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6 (ballcocks; anti-siphon requirement); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Which of the following is the most important fixture in a janitor's room?
n: A slop (service) sink, a floor-mounted sink for filling and emptying mop buckets, is the key fixture in a janitor's room. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions (Service Sink); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: A waterproof receptacle, typically located underground, used to store water for domestic and consumptive purposes in households or buildings.
n: A cistern is a waterproof receptacle, usually underground, that stores water for domestic use. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: An elevated structure supporting a water tank constructed at a height sufficient to pressurize a water distribution system.
n: A water tower is an elevated structure holding a tank high enough to pressurize a distribution system by gravity. Source: AWWA M42 (Steel Water-Storage Tanks); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Water fails to reach the upper floors of a building despite the presence of water in the distribution system. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
n: If the system has water but none reaches the upper floors, the pressure is too low to overcome the static head (height). Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (water supply pressure); Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6.

q: A developer plans to supply a 40-hectare subdivision using a ground reservoir and an elevated water tank. The terrain varies by ±12 meters, with the highest natural point located near the geometric center of the service area. To ensure uniform static pressure, minimize pump cycling, and reduce friction losses across the distribution grid, where should the elevated water tank ideally be located?
o: At the highest natural elevation near the subdivision's center, allowing gravity to provide uniform pressure and reducing reliance on continuous pumping
Adjacent to the main access road regardless of elevation, to simplify maintenance logistics and reduce construction cost
At the lowest point of the subdivision to maximize suction head for the pumps and stabilize downstream pressure fluctuations
At the farthest boundary of the subdivision to ensure that the longest pipe run receives the highest possible pressure
n: An elevated tank at the highest ground near the center gives the most uniform gravity pressure and the shortest, balanced pipe runs, which cuts pumping and friction losses. Source: AWWA M32 (Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems); PD 957/BP 220 Revised IRR (water supply).

q: It provides a relaxing and serene shower as it sprays water down vertically. Its showerhead is large and typically ranges from 8 to 20 inches.
n: A rain shower has a large overhead head, typically 8–20 in., that drops water vertically like rainfall. Source: Plumbing fixture catalogs (rain showerheads).

q: Typically placed below or at the termination of the downspout, it prevents the build-up of debris in the drainpipes.
n: A catch basin at or below a downspout outlet traps debris and sediment before they enter the drain pipes. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11 (Storm Drainage); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Recommended drain for a garage
n: Trench drains are long linear drains that collect runoff across a garage floor or driveway. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (floor and trench drains).

q: A valve that is integral to a submersible pump.
n: Submersible pumps have a built-in check valve that keeps water in the riser from flowing back when the pump stops. Source: Karassik, Pump Handbook; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A shut-off valve that operates quickly with just a 90-degree rotation of the handle to control the flow.
n: Quarter-turn valves (ball, butterfly, plug) open or shut with a 90° turn of the handle. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (valves); ASME B16.34.

q: Which is a quarter-turn valve?
n: A butterfly valve has a disc that turns a quarter-turn (90°) on a shaft to open or close the flow. It is compact and quick-acting, common on large pipes. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (valves).

q: Which of the following components is a self-activating device installed in general piping systems to permit flow in one direction only and prevent reverse flow, but is not designed for cross-connection control or potable water protection?
n: A check valve lets flow go one way only. It is not an approved cross-connection (backflow) protection device for potable water. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6 (cross-connection control); ASSE standards.

q: Also known as ball valves, these valves are used to immediately stop the flow of fluid. However, the fast opening and closing of the valve may cause water hammer.
n: Quick-acting shut-off (ball) valves stop flow at once. Closing them fast can cause water hammer. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (valves; water hammer).

q: {n a high-rise building, occupants report a sudden banging noise within the water distribution pipes whenever a flush valve closes rapidly. Investigation reveals thal the flowing water is. being abruptly stopped. generating a transient pressure wave through the piping system. This condition is known as
n: Water hammer is the pressure surge, heard as banging, when flowing water is stopped suddenly, for example by a fast-closing flush valve. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 6 (water hammer arresters); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: In a pressure-assisted water closet installation supplied by a 1-inch branch line at 310 kPa dynamic pressure, the flush valve must perform which primary hydraulic function to ensure complete fixture evacuation, while also complying with modern water-efficiency requirements, assuming the trapway geometry is already optimized for siphonic action?
o: Regulate downstream negative pressure to maintain a constant trap weir elevation throughout the flush cycle regardless of fixture load

Deliver a short-duration, high-velocity surge that initiates siphonic evacuation and restores the trap seal, while simultaneously metering a calibrated discharge volume to ensure controlled and efficient water usage without relying on stored head pressure
Maintain a continuous laminar flow regime through the fixture to minimize air entrainment during the refill stage and prevent turbulence-induced trap oscillation
Provide a pressure-equalization bypass that stabilizes upstream and downstream static heads during peak demand to prevent transient backflow conditions
n: A pressure-assisted flush valve gives a short, high-velocity surge that starts siphonic evacuation and refills the trap seal. It also meters a calibrated volume for efficient water use. Source: ASME A112.19.2 / A112.19.14; Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 4.

q: Also known as sluice valves, these valves allow control of the flow rate, from full flow to slow trickles to full stop. However, this valve does not allow for an immediate stop. It is prevalent in water supply systems and is very useful in isolating parts of the water supply system for maintenance, repair, new installation and rerouting the flow.
n: Gate (sluice) valves are mainly for isolating parts of a water system. They close gradually, not instantly, and are common in water supply. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (valves).

q: Which pipe is made from polypropylene random copolymer plastic, known for its high strength, durability and resistance to corrosion and chemical attack, can be used for hot and cold applications, and is usually offered in green or white color?
n: PPR pipe is made of polypropylene random copolymer. It is strong, corrosion- and chemical-resistant, suits hot and cold water, and usually comes in green or white. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 6 (Water Supply Materials); ISO 15874 (PP-R piping systems).

q: Which is a natural, non-synthetic pipe that is very durable and will not crack or crumble after many years of use? It can be used for both hot and cold applications; on the downside, it is expensive.
n: Copper is a natural, non-synthetic pipe material. It is very durable, will not crack or crumble after many years of use, and works for hot and cold water, but it is expensive. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 6; Copper Development Association, Copper Tube Handbook.

q: Which pipe is made from steel coated with zinc to protect it against corrosion and rusting, is ideal for outdoor applications as well as sprinkler systems, but is less durable than stainless steel and copper and takes more time to install?
n: Galvanized iron (GI) pipe is steel coated with zinc to resist corrosion and rust. It suits outdoor lines and sprinkler systems but is less durable than stainless steel or copper and slower to install (threaded joints). Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 6; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: Solvent cement is used to connect which type of pipes?
n: Solvent cement joins PVC and CPVC pipe. HDPE and PEX use fusion or mechanical fittings. Source: ASTM F493 (CPVC solvent cements); Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 3 (joints).

q: Rubber couplings and gear clamps are used to connect which type of pipes?
n: Hubless cast-iron pipe is joined with neoprene sleeves (rubber couplings) and stainless-steel band clamps. Source: CISPI 310; Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 3.

q: Which of the following is the best-suited material for hot water applications, ensuring both high-temperature resistance and long-term durability, while being specifically formulated for such use?
n: CPVC is PVC chlorinated specifically for hot-water service, rated to about 93 °C (200 °F). Source: ASTM D2846 (CPVC hot- and cold-water distribution).

q: Lead and oakum are used to connect which type of pipes?
n: Hub-and-spigot cast-iron joints are caulked with oakum and molten lead. Source: CISPI 301; Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 3 (caulked joints).

q: Standard color of HDPE pipes
n: HDPE pipe is standardly black: carbon black gives UV resistance. Colored stripes can mark the service. Source: AWWA C906; ASTM D3350.

q: You are specifying materials for a high-pressure discharge line connected to a variable-speed booster pump. The project requires a seamless pipe with no longitudinal welds, uniform wall strength, and high resistance to cyclic pressure fatigue to prevent leak development over time. Which type of pipe best satisfies this requirement?
n: Seamless (SMLS) steel pipe has no longitudinal weld, so wall strength is uniform and fatigue resistance under cyclic pressure is high. Source: ASTM A106 / API 5L (seamless pipe).

q: Which plumbing fitting is primarily used to change the direction of flow in a piping system?
n: Elbows change the direction of flow. Tees and wyes branch it, and unions join pipes. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (fittings); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A cold-water distribution line transitions from a 32 mm pipe to a 25 mm pipe due to a branch supplying a lower-demand fixture. To maintain proper flow characteristics and ensure a secure connection between the two different pipe diameters, which fitting should be installed?
n: A reducer connects two pipes of different diameters in line, here 32 mm to 25 mm. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (pipe fittings).

q: In a concealed plumbing installation where a non-pressurized drain line must be secured directly against a masonry wall without inducing point-load deformation on the pipe, which fastening component is specifically intended to hold the pipe in place while distributing the load uniformly around its circumference?
n: A pipe clamp wraps the pipe and holds it to the wall, spreading the load around the circumference without denting it. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 3 (hangers and supports); MSS SP-58.

q: What component is typically used to cover the roughing-in of exposed piping penetrations through walls, floors, or ceilings to provide a clean, finished appearance?
n: An escutcheon is the decorative plate covering the opening where a pipe passes through a wall, floor or ceiling. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (plumbing trim); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: An electrical box that protects electrical wires at their splicing and tapping points
n: A junction box encloses and protects wires at splice and tap points. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Art. 3.14.

q: A leading manufacturer of networking cables, including CAT 6 cables.
n: Belden is a leading maker of networking cable, including Category 6. Source: Manufacturer product lines (Belden structured cabling).
